top_choice_rationale: P004 names one bounded achievement: the Jaksch-Zoller proposal and the Greiner-Bloch Mott-insulator experiment showed that ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise the Bose-Hubbard model in a controllable way, a method reproduced by many groups over two decades that changed how many-body problems are posed. I rank it first with open reservations about credit (Jaksch, Cirac and Dalibard are left out) and about overlap with the 2001 and 2012 prizes. P001 is a close second because it pairs a sharp prediction with a decisive measurement, although the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang weakens it. P002 has the cleanest credit but is the most incremental relative to 2005 and 2012. P003 follows because its experimental slot overlaps with the 2012 prize and with the 2025 quantum-circuits prize. No award ranks last, since several mature, well-credited options exist.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; his many-body and statistical-physics field proximity to the lattice-simulation proposal is noted, but no documented personal connection to the candidates.
